claims.claim: Reviewers note that specific controllers such as the PS5 DualSense and older gamepads are not detected or have mismatched key bindings.

citations.review_text:
the game booted up. wouldn't accept inputs from PS5 Duelsense controller. 

After i enabled steam inputs.. i got to training mode and with in 3 mins of training mode the game crashed. tried rebooting the game.. froze my entire PC.

reset my PC and tried again thinking it was a fluke. crashed my PC again. reset again.

tried turning off steam inputs. Game didn't allow me to play it (no input detection from Duelsense. tried closing the game... crashed my PC

Third PC reset. Updated my nvidia drivers. Game crashed on boot of easy anti cheat. loaded up the game again. got into game, but no input from Duelsense, Tried to close, crashed my PC again. Reset my PC for the 4th time

Booted up the game, crashed on Easy Anti Cheat bootup. tried again and loaded the game while using PS4 Duelshock (with no steam input). Wouldn't let me play the game (not detecting inputs at all). Tried closing the game... crashed my PC again. this is now my 5th PC reset and like the 7th game crash on boot in a total play time of 30 mins.

i already requested a refund. because why is a game that literally DOESNT work on a steam sale at all.

this was a rebuy from me moving over to PC and I couldn't be more disappointed in this port of the game. 

This will stay a negative review until these problems are resolved because how in gods name are you releasing DLC for a game that cant even boot. This has to be breaking some kind of law.

The gameplay and visuals are incredibly good. Beyond that, this is a terrible game. The menu and lobby is terrible. Limited gamepad support; my Dualshock 2 isn't detected. Instead, I had to switch to my 8bitdo ultimate controller to play, but the key bindings are not matching. How hard can it be to make gamepad key bindings universal? 

The story is annoying and boring. Clicking through the dialogue is a chore for story progression; almost as bad as the North American edition of the stretched out DBZ show. As bad as some view the DBZ: Kakarot game, at least the menu was easier to work through and you could figure out how to play the game immediately; a much better tutorial than what they offer in this game.

With all the positive reviews, I expected more from this game. At this moment, I cannot recommend this game. DBZ: Kakarot at least lets you play the original stories and the fighting is easy and fun.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the game as a complex, hardcore competitive fighting game that demands extensive practice rather than a simple casual experience.

citations.review_text:
The Combat and Graphics were amazing but damn are they going to throw 50 different techniques at you and I was expecting something a little more simple like Smash Bros, when this is just as complicated as most PVP 2d Fighting games. 

This is not the Budokai series in 2d but a hardcore competitive fighter that thrives on hours and hours of practice.

The good thing is that its a fighting game and the bad thing is that it is a fighting game. To me, as a non fighting game player, this is the anime dragonball fighting experience vs the flashy 3D dragonball fighting experience of sparkling zero and vs the custom character dragonball experience of xenoverse 2. However, as a non fighting game player, it is an impossibly hard game to learn if you want to maximize what you can do. Which is a good thing and a bad thing. If you are looking for a serious fighting game to sink time into mastering, this is great. However, if you are a casual dragonball player like me, maybe not so. But i am still giving it a thumbs up.

cohorts.label: 2-20h
cohorts.summary: The striking visual presentation draws praise, while startup crashes, online desyncs, and brutal matchmaking challenge newcomers.

claims.claim: The game does not launch natively on the Steam Deck and requires third-party tools like ProtonUp-Qt to run.

citations.review_text:
I love this game. It is one of my favorite games. Some of the best memories with game buds were made here... On PS4.

Natively, this game does not even launch on steamdeck (maybe Linux in general) even with SteamOS's built-in compatibility layers. There is a fix, and it works fine. Download ProtonUp-Qt > install latest proton version > relaunch steam > launch DBFZ. Cool. All systems nominal. Even online works!... Until I get booted due to anti-cheat discriminating against Linux.

This is a long known issue and probably the final plague to Linux gaming. Arcsys, Bandai, PLEASE REMEDY THIS!!! Other multiplayer games have solved this (The Finals, for example) and it would significantly add to the playerbase if Linux and Steamdeck were officially supported. 

Downheartedly, I cannot recoomend this game while it neglects the Linux playerbase. Thank you for the memories and thrills, I'd love to have more, but y'all won't let me :\
Unplayable on the Steam Deck.

claims.claim: Players experience recurring fatal error crashes on startup that require deleting localappdata files to bypass.

citations.review_text: After playing for 6 hours and restarting the game the next day I'm am met with a fatal error crash every time I start the game. You can delete localappdata and it lets the game work, but as soon as you close it and try to re-open the game you're forced to delete localappdata again. Not worth the hassle to play a fun and enjoyable 2D Dragon Ball Fighting game.

For the simple fact of this being the most visually stunning dragon ball game ever made, this gets a thumbs up.

I do think that there are also a lot of things about this game that I personally dont like, in addition to there being some insane technical issues that I cant wrap my head around.

Where do I even begin?
I got into this game super late, so I would expect that enough patching and updating would make the game stable by now. I am in awe at how every time me and two other friends queue up to do a raid boss fight the game desyncs. Its seemingly random, and never lets us finish a run to clear. We keep attempting a 7 round super hard, and at any random point in time one of us will say "oh man you just stood still and died" but on another screen the fight is still going strong. We've made up games to try and race to see who wins their pocket dimension fight first. The second a match on anyones screen finishes it stops everyones screens and puts us back in the waiting room to the next fight and everything is still jumbled up and broken. One of us could be on fight 5/7 and the other two are still on 3/7. Its honestly impressive how hard the game can break doing these. I did some digging and saw that its a very common issue on all platforms including console, and can even extend into 1v1 pvp fights! Desyncs being so common is just flat unacceptable this late into the lifespan.

Aside from that, I kinda just dont enjoy that a lot of this games flow boils down to "I pressed one button a few times and got a combo that led into a super". Im not even being sarcastic, a singular button can do a combo into a super with no extra input for many characters. There is also a universal bread n butter combo applicable to every character (except i think maybe one?) and that feels pretty bad for variety when all thats said about starting any character is being directed to learn this combo. There is deeper combat and mindgames here but the flow being like this aint for me, especial…

claims.claim: Online multiplayer matches pit newcomers against highly experienced players, making the beginner online experience discouraging.

citations.review_text: due to how old the game is becoming a new player (at least online) is borderline impossilbe. every single bottom tier match is someone with a fresh account (no matches) and with the skill level of high tier players. if the smurfing wasn't so previlent the game might be viable but atleast for now if you are new, play offline.

This game is just as cool as when it first released. The graphics are incredible. The character roster is not perfect, but it's more than passable. The system is easy to learn, and hard to master. Overall, good game.

However, if you're buying it *for the first time*, I would just fully recommend against it. While the combat system has beginner-friendly bits and bobs attached, the majority of people who still play this game are people who've been playing it for hundreds, if not thousands of hours. This makes just about any online play discouraging and frustrating, especially if you're just starting out.

Now, I know what you're thinking. "Just don't play online." But, the problem is that the online modes make up the vast majority of what there is to do. If you don't battle people online, you're either going to be practicing, mashing your way through arcade mode a few times, or playing the frankly horrendous story mode.

Bottom line, if you want to invest e-sports levels of time into the game to get good, then go for it. If you can handle that, the game is incredible (aside from the borked story mode). But, if you're at all looking for a fun, casual time, or this would be your first fighting game experience, stay far away.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the game as having high visual quality and accurate art style representing the anime series.

citations.review_text: Absolute peak visual fan service paired with surprisingly deep, fast-paced tag fighting. Pulling off cinematic level 3 supers never gets old, and the mechanical skill ceiling is much higher than you'd expect from an anime fighter. The netcode used to hold it back, but if you love the series or classic 3v3 fighters, it’s an easy recommend.

Bar none, one of the best anime video game experiences ever created.

It is so good and so respectful to the DRAGON BALL franchise, you would think Akira Toriyama possessed the team to create this fighting game.

It is so energizing, that even when looking at perfect-looking cutscenes, you feel like teleported back to being a kid, watching this series for the first time.

This was Arc System Works in their animalistic prime. Pure artistic, technical mastery and wizardry.

Only thing more meaningful than to master this fighting game in your lifetime is to hit your head against a brick wall, it is that end result of perfection.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the story mode as unappealing or uninteresting.

citations.review_text:
I believe that this game needs a serious overhaul with the matchmaking system in it; it is one of the WORST wait times I have ever experienced for a game. I have tried multiple times to get into this title, but the matchmaking system simply does not work. This is my main complaint, the rest of this review is just my personal opinion/experience as a gamer [with 25 years of experience.] 

In terms of the matches you do manage to get into online; if you don't have your combo's absolutely perfect you're just going to be steam rolled due to their being 0 margin for error. Including no matching or options for facing new players. 

The writing for the story is interesting at best; it takes a long time to complete it with a system of rinse and repeating fights. I believe there is no purpose getting into this title unless you have experience or a friend who also plays, or just flat out have a lot of time on your hands. The DLC is incredibly expensive as well. Dragonball Z has an incredible story and unique characters, but there are other titles that offer a better experience than this one. 

The devs did an incredible job with attention to detail with the characters design, dialog, and costume design. But these other issues lead me to saying do not purchase this without these things in mind.

the gameplay is addictively entertaining. the story mode of this game is lowkey garbage, I wouldn't suggest it. the online is a waste unless you already have friends with this game already. combat is easy to learn and takes A LOT to master (it gets ridiculous once you and/or your opponent is fighting at high skill levels... beginners will also have a lot of fun too in their own easy to play way).

the main mode for me was the arcade, where I could sink hours and hours of my time in a day without fail. it starts out easy, however the hard modes of the first three (pretty easy) stages, get so diabolically difficult yet engaging that you would get absolutely demolished, restart, and go try again over and over. challenge is not hard to find, and it's great to play right after coming from work or school when you want to wind down (or up, if that's what you're into), and mindlessly play battles that challenge you and keep you entertained consistently without crazy investment. it helps that the visuals of this game are absolutely gorgeous. the ultimate moves alone are spectacle to witness. 

9/10 game. fully suggest it. it's a phenomenal fighting game.
you could buy the full game right now and easily have fun or wait for their discount special where they sell the fighterz edition for dirt cheap (comes with the full DLC 1 pack) if you want more characters from the jump and you are willing to wait for the bandai namco steam sales

A truly spectacular fighting game that I believe does the best job of adapting the Dragon Ball franchise into a video game. I got this game on sale a couple years ago and I still think its a great experience in 2026. If you are new to fighting games, I would either plan on putting some time into this one or pick it up with some friends to all learn because online is definitely rough to start. 

If you end up enjoying the core gameplay and putting some time in though this has got to be one of the most engaging fighting games I've ever played. Learning the basics of air combos, working in assists, and finally pulling off a crazy combo in a real match feels so rewarding. The gameplay just feels fantastic and the animations are so damn cool.

If this game is on sale I would absolutely pick it up, especially if you can get some friends to play with. Nothing beats improving together and watching everyone grow into their own playstyles/characters. Highly recommend!

claims.claim: Reviewers state that Easy Anti-Cheat prevents online play for Linux users or those using mods such as controller icons.

citations.review_text:
Uses EAC in a way that prevents online play if you want mods (even just Dual Shock icons) or are on Linux.
Game runs on Linux only via GE-Proton (not the native Steam one) but that triggers EAC if you play online against someone with LeGiTiMaTe install (that is to say, unmodded on Windows).

Also new character (Daima SS4) feels more like mod than actual character with plenty of reused assets.

This game is very fast paced. It keeps you moving all the time considering everything that can happen on screen at any given moment. I'll be honest, the learning curve is a bit steep from beginner to pro. Even intermidiate level takes a while to achieve. But to give credit, this is the best-looking anime-style fighting game that I've seen, mostly regarding its reference to the anime and manga of Dragon ball series. This game has some of the best character and projectile animations. The combos look amazing and feel very rewarding when completing them, even more so when you win. The multiplier has its things like any fighting game played online but its a good expirience, I like the colored square system, the ranking system, and matchmaking is pretty decent.

This game requires your reactions quite a lot, the faster the reactions the better the plays will be. This is a very competitive game, if you wish to dive deeper into the worlds of DBFZ and the FGC, I highly recommend it! Even if some of the characters, especially the DLC, have certain moves and special attacks that can sometimes break the rules of the mechanics entirely, I'd still say for you to give it a try. This game could do with some more balancing, but overall I believe it's in a good state right now. 

I believe that this will keep gaining more popularity in the coming years for its competitive scene in the FGC. Especially now after EVO France. (06/19/26)
